quests.instruction: Leo and Priya are both picked to give a speech to the whole school. Leo grins and asks to go first. Priya's hands shake as she rereads her note cards. Which feeling fits Priya best?
quests.hint: Do not use Leo's feeling. Use Priya's clues only.
quests.explanation: Shaking hands and rereading her notes show that Priya is nervous about speaking. Leo's grin shows a different feeling about the same event.
quests.funFact: The same event can bring excitement for one person and nerves for another.

quests.instruction: Anil and Rosa both enter the district spelling contest. Anil talks happily about the new words he will learn. Rosa keeps asking, 'What if I lose in front of everyone?' How might Anil feel?
quests.hint: Ignore Rosa's worry. What is Anil talking about?
quests.explanation: Anil is looking forward to what he will learn, which fits excitement. Rosa's 'What if' questions show worry about the same contest.
quests.funFact: Some people enjoy competition, and others prefer to take part without winning being the goal.

quests.instruction: A rainstorm cancels the zoo trip. Sam kicks the floor and says, 'We waited so long!' Nina takes out a book and says, 'Good, now I can finish my chapter.' What is Nina likely feeling?
quests.hint: Nina's words and actions are different from Sam's.
quests.explanation: Nina is happy to read instead, so content fits her. Sam's kicking and words show disappointment about the same cancelation.
quests.funFact: A canceled plan can feel like a loss to one person and a gift of free time to another.

quests.instruction: Teacher changes the seats. Ravi moves next to his best friend and beams. Tessa has to leave her friends and stares at her new desk without a word. How might Tessa feel?
quests.hint: Think about what each child gained or lost.
quests.explanation: Tessa lost the seat near her friends and goes quiet, which fits disappointment. Ravi gained something, so his feeling is different.
quests.funFact: Seat changes can feel very different depending on who is moving next to whom.

quests.instruction: A puppy arrives at home. Kiara kneels and laughs as it licks her face. Her brother Dean stays by the door, arms folded, watching the puppy sniff around. What is Dean most likely feeling?
quests.hint: Look at where Dean is standing and what his arms are doing.
quests.explanation: Staying near the door with folded arms suggests Dean is not comfortable with the new puppy yet. Kiara's laughter shows how differently two people can feel about a new pet.
quests.funFact: Some people need time to warm up to new animals, and that is okay.

quests.instruction: Two friends sleep over for the first time. Mira jumps on the sofa shouting, 'This is the best!' Jo whispers, 'I think I miss my own bed...' How might Jo feel?
quests.hint: Use only Jo's words.
quests.explanation: Missing his own bed and home is homesickness. Mira's excitement shows how the same sleepover can feel different.
quests.funFact: Many people feel a little homesick at a sleepover, especially the first time.

quests.instruction: On results day, Ishaan scans the list, finds his name high up, and exhales a long breath. Kavya finds hers lower than she hoped and presses her lips together. Which feeling fits Ishaan best?
quests.hint: What does the long breath out tell you?
quests.explanation: A long exhale after finding a good result shows relief that a worry ended. Kavya's pressed lips show that the same list brought her a different feeling.
quests.funFact: Waiting for results is hard for many people, whatever the result is.

quests.instruction: At school play auditions, Pablo bounces on his toes: 'I hope I get the villain!' Hana hides behind the curtain, whispering, 'I only came to hold the script.' How might Hana feel?
quests.hint: Think about where Hana is and what she says.
quests.explanation: Hiding behind the curtain and saying she only came to hold the script show that Hana feels shy about being seen. Pablo's bounce shows the opposite.
quests.funFact: Shy people can be wonderful at helping behind the scenes.

quests.instruction: Two students stand with their poster in front of the class. Lia points proudly at the graph. Ben keeps his eyes on the floor and hides his face behind the poster. Which feeling fits Ben best?
quests.hint: Notice what Ben does with the poster.
quests.explanation: Hiding his face behind the poster and looking at the floor suggest Ben feels embarrassed about being looked at. Lia's pride is about the same presentation.
quests.funFact: Many people feel embarrassed when everyone's eyes are on them.

quests.instruction: Two cousins get new haircuts. Zia runs to the mirror, turning her head and smiling. Raj touches his head and says quietly, 'It is shorter than I wanted.' Which feeling fits Zia best?
quests.hint: Look at what Zia does at the mirror.
quests.explanation: Turning her head and smiling at the mirror show Zia is delighted with the cut. Raj's quiet comment shows a different feeling about the same haircut.
quests.funFact: Two people can look at the same thing and like it very differently.

quests.instruction: The ferry rocks as it leaves the dock. Mohan stands at the rail with bright eyes, pointing at the waves. Anya grips the seat with both hands and keeps her eyes on the shore. How might Anya feel?
quests.hint: Use Anya's grip and where she looks.
quests.explanation: Gripping the seat and fixing her eyes on the shore suggest Anya feels unsafe on the rocking boat. Mohan's bright eyes show he does not feel that way.
quests.funFact: If you feel unsafe, it is okay to tell a grown-up and move to a steadier spot.

quests.instruction: The class votes for a leader and Tara's name wins. She smiles broadly and shakes hands. Omar looks at the votes and nods slowly, his eyes lowered. Which feeling fits Tara best?
quests.hint: Focus on Tara's smile and handshakes.
quests.explanation: A broad smile and handshakes after winning a vote show pride. Omar's lowered eyes show that the same result feels different to him.
quests.funFact: Both winning and not winning can feel big. Kind words from others help in either case.

quests.instruction: Two siblings wait at the dentist. Dara flips through a magazine. Nilu perches on the edge of her chair, tapping her foot and asking, 'How long will it take?' Which feeling fits Nilu best?
quests.hint: Use Nilu's clues, not Dara's.
quests.explanation: Tapping a foot and asking how long show Nilu feels nervous. Dara's relaxed reading shows that the same waiting room can feel calm to someone else.
quests.funFact: Asking questions beforehand can make a doctor's visit feel less unknown.

quests.instruction: At the temple festival the crowd is huge. Ria lights up and pushes forward to see the drums. Her grandmother grips her hand tight, eyes darting around. What is her grandmother most likely feeling?
quests.hint: Think about why she holds Ria's hand so tightly.
quests.explanation: A tight grip and darting eyes suggest she is worried about keeping Ria safe in the crowd. Ria's excitement shows a different view of the same crowd.
quests.funFact: Agreeing on a meeting spot ahead of time helps families feel safer in crowds.

quests.instruction: At the dinosaur exhibit, Eli reads every label aloud with his nose nearly touching the glass. Sam leans on the railing, kicking his heel and saying, 'Can we go?' How might Sam feel?
quests.hint: Sam's words and his posture matter here.
quests.explanation: Leaning, kicking his heel, and asking to leave show Sam is bored. Eli's careful reading shows the same exhibit grabs other people's interest.
quests.funFact: People are interested in different things, and that is what makes sharing interests fun.

quests.instruction: Mira's team loses the final by a single point. Mira laughs and says, 'Good game!' Ken throws down his cap and stomps off. How might Ken feel?
quests.hint: Think about Ken's actions, not Mira's.
quests.explanation: Throwing his cap and stomping off show frustration about the result. Mira's laughing shows a different reaction to the same loss.
quests.funFact: Taking a short walk can help when feelings feel too big after a game.

quests.instruction: Zoe and Jaden learn they must present together on Monday. Zoe says, 'We have got this.' Jaden says, 'But we have not even started!' and rubs his forehead. Which feeling fits Zoe best?
quests.hint: Focus on what Zoe says, not on how Jaden reacts.
quests.explanation: 'We have got this' shows confidence. Jaden's rubbing his forehead and listing the problem show worry about the same task.
quests.funFact: A confident teammate can help a worried one by breaking the work into small steps.

quests.instruction: On the first train ride across the state, Abbas presses his face to the window and counts the stations. Eila holds her seat and whispers, 'It is so loud.' What is Abbas most likely feeling?
quests.hint: Look at what Abbas is doing with his face and his counting.
quests.explanation: Pressing his face to the window and counting stations show that Abbas is interested and wants to see more. Eila's whisper shows a different reaction to the same ride.
quests.funFact: Counting stations or landmarks is a fun way to follow a journey.

quests.instruction: Uncle Ben arrives unannounced. Lena runs to hug him, laughing. Her brother Pete goes quiet and whispers, 'We did not clean up.' How might Pete feel?
quests.hint: Think about what Pete is concerned about.
quests.explanation: Pete is worried about how the messy room looks, which is embarrassment. Lena is only thinking about seeing her uncle.
quests.funFact: People care about different things when guests arrive, like the hug or the clean room.

quests.instruction: The coach announces a new player will join the team. Marcus says, 'Great, more help!' Dan crosses his arms and mutters, 'Now I will get less playing time.' Which feeling fits Dan best?
quests.hint: Dan's words tell you what he is thinking.
quests.explanation: Dan is concerned about losing playing time, which is worry. Marcus focuses on the benefits, so his feeling is different.
quests.funFact: Talking to the coach about a worry can help clear it up.

quests.instruction: At camp, Seema pats the horse's neck and asks when she can ride. Tim stands stiff beside the fence and says, 'You go first.' What is Seema most likely feeling?
quests.hint: Which child is moving toward the horse and asking for a turn?
quests.explanation: Seema is petting the horse and asking when she can ride, so she is eager. Tim's stiff stance and 'You go first' show nervousness.
quests.funFact: Trying something with a friend can help someone feel braver.

quests.instruction: In cooking class the teacher says each group must invent a new recipe. Sia claps, 'Yes!' Tomas stares at the empty bowl and says, 'I do not know where to start.' How might Tomas feel?
quests.hint: What does Tomas say about starting?
quests.explanation: Not knowing where to start is confusion. Sia's clap shows that the same task feels exciting to her.
quests.funFact: Breaking a big task into the first small step can help someone who feels stuck.

quests.instruction: In the penalty shootout, Bina is picked to take the last kick. She nods firmly and walks forward. Rick, who was not picked, bites his nails and watches. Which feeling fits Bina best?
quests.hint: Look at how Bina moves and what she does.
quests.explanation: Nodding firmly and walking forward show confidence. Rick's nail-biting shows that the same moment feels different for someone watching.
quests.funFact: Even confident people can feel butterflies. Confidence means trusting your preparation.

quests.instruction: Two teams tie for first place in the quiz. Rina hugs her teammates. Her teammate Sol is quiet and says, 'I wanted us to beat them outright.' How might Sol feel?
quests.hint: Listen to what Sol wished for.
quests.explanation: Sol wanted a clear win and got a tie, so disappointed fits. Rina is happy with the tie, so the same result means something different to each.
quests.funFact: Different people have different hopes about the same result.

quests.instruction: A family visits the village for the first time since the flood. Maya runs down the lane laughing. Her father walks slowly, touching the wall of a damaged house. What might Maya's father feel?
quests.hint: Think about what the house might mean to him.
quests.explanation: Touching the wall of a damaged house and walking slowly suggest sadness about what was lost. Maya's laughter shows her different experience of the same place.
quests.funFact: Places can hold different memories for different people.

quests.instruction: The spelling test comes back with a red mark on the last word. Lakshmi shrugs, 'Oh well, I will learn it.' Hamza taps his head and mutters, 'I knew it! Why did I forget?' Which feeling fits Hamza best?
quests.hint: Use Hamza's words and gesture.
quests.explanation: Tapping his head and asking himself why he forgot show frustration with himself. Lakshmi's shrug shows a calmer reaction to the same mark.
quests.funFact: Everyone forgets things sometimes. Kind self-talk helps a mistake feel smaller.

quests.instruction: On the hottest sports day of the year, Tia fills her water bottle and says, 'Let us go!' Omar finds a patch of shade and says, 'I cannot, it is too hot.' How might Omar feel?
quests.hint: Think about how heat affects the body.
quests.explanation: Searching for shade and saying he cannot continue show that Omar is worn out by the heat. Tia's energy shows that people handle heat differently.
quests.funFact: Resting in shade and drinking water are good ways to take care of your body in heat.

quests.instruction: Two children go through the same event and feel different things. Which explanation makes the most sense?
quests.correctAnswer: Each person brings different experiences and thoughts to the event 🧠
options: One of them must be pretending to feel something they do not 🎭
Each person brings different experiences and thoughts to the event 🧠
Only one of them can be feeling the right way about it ✅
quests.hint: Think about why two people might see the same situation differently.
quests.explanation: People bring their own experiences, thoughts, and needs to every event. That is why feelings can differ even when the event is identical.
quests.funFact: Feelings are not right or wrong. They are reactions to how a person experiences something.

quests.instruction: Jo is excited about tomorrow's match and Lee is nervous about the same match. Which statement is the most accurate?
quests.correctAnswer: Both feelings are possible, and neither one is wrong ⚽
options: If Jo is excited about the match, Lee should be excited too 📢
One of them must be confused about what the match means ❓
Both feelings are possible, and neither one is wrong ⚽
quests.hint: Look for the statement that respects both children.
quests.explanation: Different people can have different feelings about the same event, and each feeling makes sense for that person.
quests.funFact: Sharing your feelings with a teammate can help you both feel supported.

quests.instruction: During a scary movie scene, you giggle while your friend grips a cushion and looks away. What is the kindest thing to do?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask if she wants to pause or skip the scene ⏸️
options: Ask if she wants to pause or skip the scene ⏸️
Keep watching the screen and ignore what she is doing 📺
Tell her to stop being silly because it is only a film 😆
quests.hint: Think about what your friend might feel and what would help her.
quests.explanation: You notice she is uncomfortable and you offer a choice. That shows that you value her feelings even though yours are different.
quests.funFact: Offering options is a good way to include friends who feel differently from you.
